description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of question types across difficulty levels – easy, medium, and hard – as related to knowledge crossword geometric reasoning with large language models. The chart consists of three pie charts, each representing a difficulty level, and each pie chart is divided into multiple slices. The “easy” pie chart has four slices labeled “N+K+” (light green, 40.6%), “N+K-” (light orange, 10.1%), “N-K+” (yellow, 45.9%), and “N-K-” (red, 3.3%). The “medium” pie chart also has four slices labeled “N+K+” (light green, 44.6%), “N+K-” (light orange, 7.2%), “N-K+” (yellow, 44.3%), and “N-K-” (red, 3.9%). The “hard” pie chart has five slices labeled “N+K+” (light green, 36.2%), “N+K-” (light orange, 20.1%), “N-K+” (yellow, 36.8%), “N-K-” (red, 7.0%), and an additional slice labeled “N+K” (teal, 10.1%). Each pie chart includes percentage labels displayed within the slices, and a legend is provided below the charts to identify the labels. The slices within each pie chart appear to be ordered clockwise by decreasing size.
